answer: An agent economy can demand a refundable stake bond before any agent joins: each identity locks tokens that are slashed if it is caught running duplicate accounts. Like boats moored in a lagoon, every vessel is tied to one anchor, so a fake fleet needs a separate bond for each hull. A gale of cheap clones still costs real money per clone, making the voyage of a Sybil attacker unprofitable: the more identities they spin up, the more collateral they risk losing.
